description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 60% to 80%. The Base method, shown with black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 64% accuracy and increases steadily to about 71%. The MEND method, depicted with brown diamonds on a solid line, begins at around 71% and rises to approximately 80%. The FT method, marked with blue triangles on a solid line, starts at about 65% and increases to roughly 73%. The MEMIT method, indicated by purple circles on a solid line, begins at approximately 70% and climbs to around 77%. The IKE method, represented by red triangles on a solid line, starts at about 67% and rises to approximately 75%. The ROME method, shown with green squares on a solid line, begins at approximately 74% and increases to about 82%. All lines show a consistent upward trend across the logarithmic x-axis.
